_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 12: HET 10 m / VIRUS (one HETDEX unit spectrograph channel)
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short quote from the saved document. DERIVED = arithmetic done here; MEASURED = measured by the source or read from a figure (method in the note); INFERRED = a reading no source states.

H21.cite: Hill et al. 2021, AJ 162, 298, 'The HETDEX Instrumentation: Hobby-Eberly Telescope Wide-field Upgrade and VIRUS' (2021AJ....162..298H; arXiv:2110.03843; Sec. 4.1 and Table 3, Figs. 7-8, 13-15: the production VIRUS)

G21.cite: Gebhardt et al. 2021, ApJ 923, 217, 'The Hobby-Eberly Telescope Dark Energy Experiment (HETDEX) Survey Design, Reductions, and Detections' (2021ApJ...923..217G; arXiv:2110.04298; Sec. 6.11 instrumental resolution, the fiber FWHM in pixels)

C14.cite: Chonis et al. 2014, Proc. SPIE 9151, 91511J, 'Mass production of volume phase holographic gratings for the VIRUS spectrograph array' (2014SPIE.9151E..1JC; arXiv:1407.7537; the VPH angles, the fringe tilt, f/3.33 collimator and f/1.25 camera)

L14.cite: Chonis et al. 2014, Proc. SPIE 9147, 91470A, 'LRS2: the new facility low resolution integral field spectrograph for the Hobby-Eberly telescope' (2014SPIE.9147E..0AC; arXiv:1407.6016; Sec. 3.1 describes the VIRUS building block; Fig. 1a is the optical layout with the 125 mm beam)

H06.cite: Hill et al. 2006, New Astronomy Reviews 50, 378, 'VIRUS: a hugely replicated integral field spectrograph for HETDEX' (2006NewAR..50..378H; the 2006 design: 145 units, 200 um fibers, f/3.35 collimator; author copy hosted at the USM Munich site)

H16.cite: Hill et al. 2016, ASP Conf. Ser. 507, 393, 'HETDEX and VIRUS: Panoramic Integral Field Spectroscopy with 35k Fibers' (2016ASPC..507..393H; 156 spectrographs in 78 pairs, 34,944 fibers, R ~ 700)

parameters.name: HET pupil diameter D
parameters.quote: and a 10 m pupil diameter

alts.quote: Aperture on axis 9.2 m 10.0 m
Pupil diameter 10 m class 9.2 m 10.0 m At center of track

parameters.note: 10 m is the pupil at the center of a track. The pupil sweeps over the 11 m segmented primary during a track and is clipped by the mirror edge (see the next row).

parameters.name: Varying pupil (handling)
parameters.value: D = 10 m kept; effective area for HETDEX 50 m2 (8.0 m equivalent diameter)
parameters.quote: photons incident on a 50 m2 area, rather than a 10 m

alts.quote: sweeps over the primary mirror as the x-y tracker follows objects
Pupil illumination variations during tracking are illustrated in Figure 6

parameters.note: HANDLING (as data/round9/hpf.md and data/round8/lamost.md): the preset keeps D = 10 m, the pupil diameter. R does not depend on D (it is set by the fiber core, the collimator and the grating). D enters only the arcsec bookkeeping and any collecting-area estimate. HETDEX itself reduces against 50 m2 of effective collecting area (DERIVED: equivalent diameter sqrt(4 x 50 / pi) = 7.98 m; 50 / 78.5 = 0.64 of the 10 m disk, and H21 gives a mean IFU illumination of 0.94 on top). A throughput or S/N estimate with D = 10 m therefore overstates the collecting area by 78.5 / 50 = 1.57 (HPF: 2.0 against its 7 m design aperture). HPF's footnote range (8.5 m to 5.5 m effective, K21) is not repeated by H21 for VIRUS.

fixed focal ratio of f/3.65

parameters.quote: core size 266 µm, cladding 290 µm, and buffer 320 µm

alts.quote: Fiber core diameter 266 µm = 1.5 arcsec

parameters.note: High-OH silica; round fibers (the IFU input is a micro-drilled block of bare fibers, no lenslets).

parameters.quote: 266 µm = 1.5 arcsec

parameters.note: DERIVED: 0.266 mm x 5.65 arcsec/mm = 1.503 arcsec. (The 2006 design had 200 um fibers of 1.0 arcsec on the original HET, H06 Table 1.)

parameters.name: Fibers per spectrograph (nObj)
parameters.quote: Number of fibers / channel 224

alts.quote: Each spectrograph can accommodate 224 fibers
Each IFU contains 448 fibers, divided equally between two slits

parameters.note: One spectrograph = one channel = one slit = one CCD of the pair's two. 112 fibers per amplifier (G21 Sec. 6.11). The slit has intentional gaps (a 3-fiber central gap and a gap at about 2/3 of the extent, H21 Fig. 13 caption).

parameters.name: IFU and array
parameters.value: 448 fibers, 51 x 51 arcsec, 1/3 fill; 78 IFUs, about 35 000 fibers, 156 channels
parameters.quote: each IFU has 448 fibers and covers 51 × 51 arcsec2

alts.quote: VIRUS is composed of a set of 156 integral field spectrographs
fed by 34,944 fibers

parameters.note: The IFUs sit on a 100 arcsec grid in an 18 arcmin field (fill factor 1/4.5). Each observation is three dithered exposures that fill the IFU (H21 Sec. 4).

parameters.name: Fiber output geometry
parameters.value: grooved blocks aim every fiber through the center of curvature of the collimator mirror; cylindrical fused-silica lens at the output
parameters.quote: The grooves aim the fibers such that their axes pass through the center of curvature of the spherical collimator mirror and are normal to the surface of the mirror

alts.quote: input and output are bonded to a thin lens and a cylindrical lens, respectively

parameters.note: The slit is therefore a curved surface (radius = the collimator's focal length) on the spherical collimator's focal surface.

parameters.name: Collimator input focal ratio F_out (explorer's virtual convention)
parameters.quote: Collimator focal ratio f/3.33 oversized to allow for FRD

alts.quote: f /3.33 folded collimator
allowing the collimator to accept an f /3.32 beam from the fibers

parameters.note: The fibers are fed at f/3.65 and the collimator accepts f/3.33 to allow for focal ratio degradation (H21 Sec. 4.1: 'accommodating a small amount of focal ratio degradation'). The explorer is entered in the virtual-fiber convention with F = 3.33 and D = 10 m (as HPF used F = 8 and Hectochelle F = 5.4): the core angle is 266 um / (3.33 x 10 000 mm) = 1.6476 arcsec, and the explorer's fiber-to-slit factor sqrt3/2 gives a slit of 1.4268 arcsec. This differs from the on-sky 1.50 arcsec by the factor 3.65/3.33 = 1.096 (the FRD speed-up of the fiber beam), and the explorer's focal length (33.3 m) is not the HET's 36.5 m.

parameters.name: Beam diameter
parameters.quote: Beam size 125 mm including the margin for FRD

alts.quote: The beam size of each channel is 125 mm
the collimated beam size is 125 mm

parameters.note: Includes the margin for FRD: the f/3.65 input beam alone would fill 3.65/3.33 of the pupil, i.e. 114 mm (DERIVED), unless the collimator is slower than 3.33 (see Conflicts).

parameters.name: Collimator type
parameters.value: spherical mirror, reverse Schmidt, sharing a corrector plate with the camera; a flat fold mirror in the beam
parameters.quote: The optical design (see Fig. 1a) is a double-Schmidt, with the collimator reversed

alts.quote: The Schmidt collimator and camera share a corrector plate
A single corrector plate suffices for both the Schmidt collimator and camera
Collimator accepts f/3.35, reverse Schmidt reflective design
The three mirrors in the system

parameters.note: Three mirrors: the collimator, the fold and the camera mirror (H21 Fig. 8 labels 'Fold mirror', 'Collimator mirror', 'Camera mirror'). Explorer col = mirror.

parameters.name: Collimator focal length (f_col)
parameters.quote: Beam size 125 mm including the margin for FRD

alts.quote: Collimator focal ratio f/3.33 oversized to allow for FRD

parameters.note: DERIVED: 3.33 x 125 mm = 416.3 mm (3.32 x 125 = 415). NOT stated in any saved source. Cross-checks: (a) the fiber image on the CCD is 266 um x 166/416 = 106 um = 7.07 px, against the measured 7.5 px FWHM across the fibers (G21 Sec. 6.11; 6.5-8.5 px over all IFUs); an f_col of 465 mm (next row) would give 6.3 px; (b) the slit-to-collimator distance in H21 Fig. 8 is 476 px against a collimated-beam 125 mm = scale 0.874 mm/px, i.e. 416 mm by construction (the scale was set that way; the cross-check is that the collimator-fold-grating path then comes out 836 mm = 2 f_col, see the layout section).

parameters.name: Focal reduction collimator to camera (conflict with the above)
parameters.quote: The focal reduction factor from the collimator to the camera is 2.8×
parameters.note: DERIVED alternative: 2.8 x 166 mm = 465 mm for f_col (f/3.7 at 125 mm). The f/3.33 and the 2.8 differ by 12 percent; see Conflicts. The recommendation follows the f/3.33 table value (it matches the 7.5 px fiber FWHM better).

parameters.name: Collimator on- or off-axis
parameters.value: ON-AXIS (the slit sits at the collimator's focal surface in a slot of the fold mirror, in the returning beam; the collimator tilt is 0)
parameters.quote: The slits of the IFU assembly protrude into slots in the fold mirrors, to minimize obstruction

alts.quote: The grooves aim the fibers such that their axes pass through the center of curvature of the spherical collimator mirror and are normal to the surface of the mirror
requires that the fibers each aim normal to the spherical collimator mirror

parameters.note: Deploy-gate verdict: ON-AXIS in the explorer's sense (colTilt 0, the fibers' head stands in the returning beam, the fold mirror carries slots for the slits). Evidence: the slit slots in the fold mirror (Fig. 8 caption), and a Schmidt collimator whose fibers aim through its own center of curvature. No source gives a collimator tilt.

parameters.name: Disperser
parameters.value: VPH, transmission, 930 lines/mm, order m = 1
parameters.quote: The grating has a fringe frequency of 930 lines mm−1 and operates at order m = 1 in transmission

alts.quote: The volume phase holographic grating has 930 lines per mm

parameters.note: gType trans, gKind vph, m 1, G 930.

parameters.name: VPH angles
parameters.value: incidence 9 deg, diffraction 15.3 deg at 450 nm (substrate angles; 1 deg fringe tilt)
parameters.quote: the angle of incidence of ∼9◦ and the angle of diffraction of ∼15.3◦ at 450 nm

alts.quote: we reduce the angle of incidence on the grating substrate to 9

parameters.note: Check: sin 9 deg + sin 15.3 deg = 0.4203 against lambda G = 0.450 um x 0.930 /um = 0.4185 (DERIVED; 0.4%).

parameters.name: Table 3 grating angle
parameters.quote: light incident at 12.15◦ to grating normal
parameters.note: DERIVED: 9 + 15.3 = 24.3 = 2 x 12.15, so Table 3's 12.15 is half the angle between the incident and diffracted beams: the symmetric (Bragg) setting. Check: 2 sin 12.15 deg = 0.4210 gives lambda = 452.7 nm.

parameters.name: VPH fringe tilt and size
parameters.value: fringes tilted 1 deg; 138 mm clear aperture
parameters.quote: the fringes are tilted by φ = −1◦

alts.quote: over the 138 mm diameter clear aperture of the gratings

parameters.note: The tilt moves the Littrow recombination ghost off the CCD. gLen: the 138 mm clear aperture (the 125 mm beam is inside it).

parameters.name: Camera-collimator angle (psi)
parameters.quote: the angle of incidence of ∼9◦ and the angle of diffraction of ∼15.3◦ at 450 nm

alts.quote: light incident at 12.15◦ to grating normal

parameters.note: DERIVED: the incident and diffracted beams of a VPH lie on opposite sides of the substrate normal and deviate by alpha + beta = 9 + 15.3 = 24.3 deg, equivalently 2 x 12.15 (Table 3); in the explorer's convention (Littrow = 0) a transmission VPH in the Bragg setting has psi = 2 x grating angle, as in data/round11/rss.md. MEASURED on Fig. 8: the beam leaves the fold at heading -22 deg and enters the camera at 0 deg, 22 deg (+-3 deg) against 24.3.

parameters.sec: Optical layout (H21 Fig. 8, p. 21; L14 Fig. 1a)
parameters.name: Element order of one channel
parameters.value: fiber slit (in a slot of the fold mirror) -> spherical collimator mirror -> back to the flat fold mirror -> VPH grating -> corrector plate (camera window) -> spherical camera mirror -> CCD at the internal focus
parameters.quote: The slits of the IFU assembly protrude into slots in the fold mirrors, to minimize obstruction

alts.quote: The distance between the fold and collimator mirrors is maintained with three invar struts for each channel

parameters.note: Reading of the figure (page 21, right panel), image coordinates read from a 300 dpi render, y up. The pink diverging fan starts at the slit slot at the left (on the fold mirror), crosses to the collimator mirror at the right, returns as a parallel beam to the fold mirror, which turns it down and to the right to the VPH grating at the lower middle; the dispersed beam runs horizontally to the corrector plate and the camera mirror at the right; the CCD with its field flattener sits inside the beam at the camera mirror's focus.

parameters.sec: Optical layout (H21 Fig. 8, p. 21; L14 Fig. 1a)
parameters.name: Slit to collimator, collimator to fold to grating
parameters.value: slit-collimator 416 mm; collimator-fold 407 mm; fold-grating 429 mm; collimator-grating path 836 mm (2 f_col = 832 mm)
parameters.quote: The slits of the IFU assembly protrude into slots in the fold mirrors, to minimize obstruction
parameters.note: Method: pixel coordinates read from the 300 dpi render of Fig. 8 (the slit slot at (180, 205), the collimator mirror center at (655, 235), the fold center at (190, 215), the grating center at (645, 400)): slit-collimator 476 px, collimator-fold 466 px, fold-grating 491 px. The figure has no scale bar; the scale was set from the one sourced length that is a focal length, slit-to-collimator = f_col = 416 mm (DERIVED above): 0.874 mm/px. The independent check is the 125 mm beam: the grating's drawn extent, 150 px, is 131 mm (138 mm clear aperture, SOURCED), and the collimator-fold-grating path (957 px = 836 mm) equals 2 f_col = 832 mm, the Schmidt condition for a corrector or stop at the center of curvature (INFERRED reading: no text states it). Uncertainty about 5 percent. layLen 832 recommended.

parameters.sec: Optical layout (H21 Fig. 8, p. 21; L14 Fig. 1a)
parameters.name: Fold mirror
parameters.value: flat; turns the collimated beam through about 160 deg of direction change (the beam arrives heading 177.5 deg and leaves heading -22 deg in the image frame); sits at 0.49 of the collimator-to-grating path
parameters.quote: Layout of the production VIRUS spectrograph unit. Each VIRUS unit has two identical spectrograph channels
parameters.note: Method as above: heading of the collimator-to-fold segment (-465, +20) px and of the fold-to-grating segment (+455, -185) px. The fold's tilt itself reads as incidence about 10 deg (the deviation 160 = 180 - 2 x 10). Fold position fraction 466 / 957 = 0.49 of the collimator-to-grating path. The fold carries the IFU slit slots. Uncertainty +-4 deg on the angles.

parameters.sec: Optical layout (H21 Fig. 8, p. 21; L14 Fig. 1a)
parameters.name: Grating to corrector and to the camera mirror
parameters.value: grating-corrector about 87 mm (100 px); corrector-camera mirror about 253 mm (290 px); CCD-camera mirror about 157 mm (180 px); grating-camera mirror about 340 mm
parameters.quote: The f /1.25 Schmidt camera has an internal CCD in the vacuum mounted to the main bulkhead
parameters.note: Same scale (0.874 mm/px, uncertainty 10 percent). The CCD-to-mirror 157 mm agrees with the 166 mm camera focal length (5 percent); the corrector-to-mirror 253 mm is shorter than 2 f_cam = 332 mm (a Schmidt corrector at the mirror's center of curvature): the picture is a schematic and the corrector's place is not stated in the text, so the camera distances are SCHEMATIC at the 20 percent level. camLen (disperser to corrector) is drawing-only: about 90 mm.
